paper.title_en: Amplitude Analysis of Di-Charmonium Resonances in Three Decay Channels
paper.abstract_en: Two narrow resonant structures at 6.9 and 7.2 GeV, as well as a broad structure near the di-$J{\kern 1pt} /{\kern 1pt} \psi $ production threshold, have recently been observed by the LHCb [1], ATLAS [2], and CMS [3] collaborations in the di-$J{\kern 1pt} /{\kern 1pt} \psi $ and $J{\kern 1pt} /{\kern 1pt} \psi $ + $\psi (2S)$ invariant-mass spectra with four muons in the final state. This suggests the existence of fully heavy tetraquark candidates with a $cc\bar {c}\bar {c}$ quark configuration: $X(6900)$, $X(7200)$, and $X(6500)$. However, their quantum properties have not yet been confirmed [4]. This report presents an amplitude analysis for the di-$J{\kern 1pt} /{\kern 1pt} \psi $ and $J{\kern 1pt} /{\kern 1pt} \psi $ + $\psi (2S)$ channels with 4μ and 4μ + 2π in final states, aimed at studying the properties of these exotic resonances. By performing a simultaneous fit to the mass and angular distributions, the masses and widths of the observed structures are determined under the hypothesis of two interfering states with ${{J}^{P}}$ = ${{0}^{ + }}$ for both. The comparisons with other spin-parity hypotheses for $X(6900)$ are also presented.
